title: The last of the Frontier Fields: Abell 370
caption: The galaxy cluster Abell 370, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This Hubble view of the galaxy cluster Abell 370 is full of arcs and streaks. They are the stretched images of galaxies lying far behind the cluster, their light bent on its way to us. The cluster itself is some five billion light-years away.

Abell 370 was one of the very first clusters where astronomers saw this effect, called gravitational lensing. The cluster's gravity warps spacetime, the fabric of space and time, and light passing through that warped region is bent and distorted, much as a curved glass lens reshapes what is seen through it.
The image came from the final observation of the Frontier Fields program, which closed with this last look at Abell 370, one of the first places where lensing was ever seen.

understand.summary: This image combines data from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys and Wide Field Camera 3, with filters from visible light into the near-infrared. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The near-infrared part of the data is invisible to the eye, and the faint background galaxies need Hubble's long exposures to appear at all.

explore: Lensed images carry information in two ways. They magnify faint background galaxies, and their shapes reveal how the cluster's mass, including unseen dark matter, is spread out.
alt: A field crowded with galaxies, with curved arcs and streaks from stretched background galaxies.
